primary_secondary.note: Industrial tool development and evaluation at Bloomberg.

study_type.claude: Mixed methods (tool development; Claude also labels it an industrial experience report)
study_type.note: The paper says 'we report on our experience at Bloomberg' and calls its evaluation mixed-methods; Experience report would also be defensible.

research_method.claude: Tool development + mixed methods: Bayesian Network modelling (literature + expert survey + HC/PC structure learning with bootstrap and BIC), performance benchmarking (Hyperfine, Locust), focus groups with post-session questionnaire
research_method.nlm: Mixed methods: literature review, expert survey, structure learning algorithms, performance benchmarking, focus groups
research_method.value: Industrial tool development and mixed-methods evaluation: two Bayesian Networks built from a DORA-based DAG, refined by an expert survey (n=8, weighted scores) and validated with Hill-Climbing/Peter-Clark structure learning (bootstrap, BIC), CPTs estimated from survey data; latency benchmarking (Hyperfine, Locust); 7 focus groups with post-session questionnaire
research_method.note: Tool names and number of focus-group sessions reported only by Claude (not contradicted).

context.claude: Industry; Bloomberg DevX team with UCL; internal survey (20 questions, >2,000 responses), 8 experts, 7 focus groups with 28 senior participants (24 respondents)
context.nlm: Industry; Bloomberg; internal survey (>2,000 responses, 20 questions), 8 DevX experts, 28 focus-group participants (24 completed questionnaire)
context.value: industry; Bloomberg (DevX team, with UCL); internal quarterly engineering survey (20 questions, >2,000 responses), 8 DevX experts, 28 senior practitioners in focus groups (24 questionnaire respondents)

dora_applied.note: DORA metrics form the foundational DAG and core nodes of the software delivery BN. Claude says the DORA nodes come from survey questions; NotebookLM says from CI/CD pipeline data (the paper builds the BNs from internal survey data).

space_applied.note: SPACE only referenced (aspects covered by the internal survey).

ai_discussed.note: Borderline: only in the sense that the proposed analysis instrument is Bayesian Networks with structure learning (HC, PC); the text never uses 'AI' or 'machine learning' outside the references, and no AI coding tools are discussed.

remote_covid.note: Work mode not specified by either.

data_window.note: Not stated by either (quarterly survey, no period given; early access since 1 Oct 2025 refers to deployment, not data).

cat_productivity.note: Borderline: both label 'time lost to obstacles' DevEx/Productivity, but it is a self-reported survey item (counted under survey); DORA throughput counted under delivery.

cat_quality.note: Change failure rate and failed deployment recovery time (stability), plus tech-debt impact survey item.

cat_collaboration.note: Claude lists 'quality of peer feedback' as a survey metric; NotebookLM has no collaboration metric. In the full text peer feedback appears once, as an intro description of survey topics, not as a BN node.

cat_satisfaction.note: Developer happiness and meaningful work are DevEx BN nodes; DevEx defined as satisfaction and engagement.

cat_activity.note: Claude lists 'contribution metrics' (internal dashboards); NotebookLM has none (its 'Activity' label is on focus without distraction). Full text mentions contribution metrics once in the intro.

cat_delivery.note: Change lead time and deployment frequency in the software delivery BN.

cat_devex.note: Claude: DevEx is the modelled domain, defined generically. NotebookLM: 'DevEx Framework' applied. Full text defines DevEx as 'satisfaction and engagement of engineers' and does not cite Noda/Storey/Forsgren; 'focus without distraction' is a survey node.

cat_agile.note: DevOps/CI/CD context only; no sprint or process metrics.

cat_survey.note: BNs built from Likert-scale internal engineering survey; tool evaluated with a post-session questionnaire.

evidence.quote: We conducted a mixed-methods evaluation of BayesInsights that combines quantitative performance benchmarking with qualitative feedback collected through a post-session survey following focus group sessions with 28 senior Bloomberg practitioners (24 of whom responded).
To further refine the DAG structures, we applied the Hill-Climbing (HC) and Peter-Clark (PC) structure-learning algorithms
We use data from one internal engineering survey (20 questions, >2,000 responses) as the source for our BNs, in which each question is represented as a graph node
Participants were purposely selected from Bloomberg's DevX team (n = 8) for their domain expertise and organisation-wide contextual understanding
We conducted seven sessions, each with 3-5 participants. In total, 28 attended the sessions, and 24 completed the questionnaire.
We began with a foundational DAG based on the DORA metrics [10] and their established causal links.
Throughput is modelled using change lead time, deployment frequency, and failed deployment recovery time, while stability is represented by change failure rate.
both time lost to obstacles and meaningful work contribute directly to developer happiness
In this context, DevEx refers to the satisfaction and engagement of engineers within their work environment.
The survey comprises Likert-scale questions capturing engineers' perceptions of their work environment, including satisfaction and engagement
